sources.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories

articles.author: Andrew Limbong
articles.description: Abdelrahman ElGendy published a recent essay about being denied a visa to enter the U.S. for the ceremony. His book is a memoir about his time as a political prisoner in Egypt.
articles.title: 'Huna' writer wins National Book Award for non-fiction, after not being allowed into the U.S.

articles.author: John Ruwitch
articles.description: The five-year-old artificial intelligence powerhouse priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, shrugging off growing concern about a possible AI bubble and volatility in tech stocks.
articles.title: Anthropic IPO raises record $81.3 billion on strong AI demand

articles.author: Jonathan Lambert
articles.description: As the emergency response to the flood ends, aid workers turn to the hard work of rebuilding communities that lost everything. Many of those workers lost everything, too.
articles.title: After Nepal's epic flood, they're restoring their community ... and their lives

articles.author: Charles Maynes
articles.description: On the sidelines of a high-powered regional economic forum in China, Presidents Trump, Xi and Putin sit down for an unprecedented meeting with nuclear non-proliferation expected to be a focus.
articles.title: Trump, Xi and Putin set to meet in historic summit

articles.author: Kirk Siegler
articles.description: Montana is sending a Democrat to the U.S. House for the first time in three decades. Many in the party think Sam Forstag's campaign may be a playbook for how Democrats can win again in rural America.
articles.title: Democratic strategists think Montana House race could hold the secret to future wins

articles.author: Brian Mann
articles.description: In a statement celebrating the historic drop in drug deaths, the White House pointed to successes since President Trump took office. In fact, the biggest progress happened under the Biden administration.
articles.title: As overdose deaths fall, White House makes misleading claims about who deserves credit

articles.author: Ruby Siefken
articles.description: On NPR's Morning Edition, fashion designer Karl Kani talks about his new memoir, dressing some of hip-hop's biggest stars and why skinny jeans aren't for everyone.
articles.title: Karl Kani dressed hip-hop royalty for decades. Now he's telling his own story

articles.author: Justin Chang
articles.description: Two films harken back to previous Oscar-winning movies. Elsinore, set in 1989 London, centers on Ian Charleson, co-star of Chariots of Fire. I Play Rocky tells the origin story of Sly Stallone's hit.
articles.title: 'I Play Rocky' and 'Elsinore' can't land their punches, even with star performances

articles.author: Amelia Edelman
articles.description: Flying somewhere for Thanksgiving or the holidays? Travel insiders explain what to do if your flight gets canceled or delayed — so you can quickly get to your destination.
articles.title: Got a canceled flight? 7 clever ways to get rebooked fast

articles.author: Elena Moore
articles.description: The New York Democrat moved a step closer to becoming the first Black lawmaker in U.S. history to serve in the job, after House Democrats voted overwhelmingly to support him.
articles.title: Democrats formally nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker of the House

articles.author: Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
If the Aboriginal woman had been checked at regular intervals as required, her ‘excess consumption of water’ would have been prevented, inquest finds
• Warning: This article contains images of and references to Indigenous Australians who have died

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The death of an Aboriginal woman who collapsed after drinking at least 20 litres of water in a New South Wales prison cell was preventable and the result of systemic failures, a coroner has found.
Tammy Michelle Shipley, 47, died at Silverwater women’s correctional centre on 20 December 2022.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tammy Shipley was supposed to be monitored in prison. Instead she died after drinking 20L of water

articles.author: Tory Shepherd
articles.description:
Inquest into deaths of four babies in northern NSW between 2022 and 2024 told mother refused to give birth in hospital after hearing others’ traumatic stories

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Baby B’s mother was so determined to have a home birth she ignored the advice of experts – including her own midwife, an inquest has heard.
The inquest heard she was pregnant with twins, which she described as a “wonderful shock”, and didn’t want a hospital birth because she had heard of others’ traumatic experiences.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mother whose twin baby died was determined to have home birth despite advice of experts, NSW inquest hears

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Modelling in draft of 10-year London plan threatens Sadiq Khan’s promises on improving air quality
Car use in London will rise by 10% over the next decade with cycling and walking falling as a proportion of trips, according to an official forecast by the city’s mayoralty, putting into doubt Sadiq Khan’s promises on air quality and the environment.
Based on projections in the draft version of the latest 10-year London plan, drawn up by the mayor’s office and Transport for London (TfL), road congestion from a growing population would slow buses down, while packed tube services might require stations to close regularly to ease numbers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Car use in London forecast to rise by 10% in next decade

articles.author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
articles.description:
Former minister, who was sentenced to prison in Bangladesh in her absence, says she was victim of ‘malicious prosecution’
The former minister Tulip Siddiq has said she is considering taking legal action against the former interim leader of Bangladesh over corruption allegations made by his administration led her to resign from the UK government last year.
The MP for Hampstead and Highgate, whose aunt Sheikh Hasina was put on trial in absentia over crimes against humanity during her 15 years as prime minister of Bangladesh, was accused of benefiting from the former regime by the authorities in the Bangladeshi capital, Dhaka.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tulip Siddiq says she is considering legal action against former Bangladesh leader

articles.author: Petra Stock
articles.description:
HMCS Spitfire was commissioned by colonial government to protect against Russian warships during the Crimean war
The wreck of Australia’s first locally built warship has been discovered 128 years after sinking off the coast of far north Queensland.
Marine archaeologists found the remains of Ex HMCS Spitfire on 21 August, the anniversary of its sinking in 1898.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Remarkable luck’: wreck of first Australian-built warship discovered exactly 128 years after sinking

articles.author: Patrick Barkham
articles.description:
Scientists use lightweight tracker to map wading bird’s extraordinary migration from Norfolk to the Arctic and back
A bar-tailed godwit called Phil has completed a 6,800-mile journey from Norfolk to Siberia and back again, in the first mapping of the endurance feats of this long-distance migrant.
A wading bird not much larger than a pigeon, the bar-tailed godwit is known for making the longest recorded non-stop migratory flight of any bird, with populations that visit Britain spending summers breeding in the Arctic Circle before retreating to the unfrozen wetlands of Britain in winter.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Meet Phil, the bar-tailed godwit tracked on a 6,800-mile round trip to Siberia

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
About 2.6m adults are taking the drugs, fuelled by the regulator’s approval of the pill versions and a rise in male users
At least one person is taking weight-loss drugs in 8.5% of households in Great Britain, according to research, meaning there are more homes with GLP-1 users than those containing vegetarians and pescatarians combined.
About 2.6 million adults were using weight-loss medication in August, a rise of about 700,000 people since February, according to a survey by Worldpanel by Numerator.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Weight-loss drugs used in nearly one in 10 homes in Great Britain, study finds

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
articles.description:
Global energy watchdog forecasts huge rise as US and China turn to fossil fuels to power AI growth agendas  
The world’s datacentres will create 70% more carbon emissions within the next four years as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to power their AI growth agendas, according to the world’s energy watchdog.
The International Energy Agency (IEA) warned that datacentres will consume twice as much electricity by 2030 compared with today, with the global expansion of artificial intelligence accounting for three-quarters of this growth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Datacentres to create 70% more carbon emissions by 2030, IEA report warns

articles.author: Sian Cain
articles.description:
Assadi’s third novel was inspired by the story of her late father, a Palestinian who escaped the Nakba as a child in 1948
Palestinian-Jewish author Hannah Lillith Assadi has won the National book award for fiction, one of the US’s most prestigious literary prizes, for her novel Paradiso 17.
Assadi’s third novel is a study of the psychic toll of displacement on migrants, through the tale of a Palestinian man who escaped the Nakba in 1948, when more than 700,000 Palestinians fled or were expelled from their homes by Israel. The story was inspired by her father, Sami Abdul-Fattah Al-Assadi, who fled the Nakba as a child with his family, before studying in Italy and moving to New York.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hannah Lillith Assadi wins National book award for ‘visionary’ novel Paradiso 17

articles.author: Catie McLeod and Jonathan Barrett
articles.description:
Australian fashion chain becomes latest retailer in trouble after David Jones, Cue and Veronika Maine

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The youth fashion chain General Pants Co has become the latest major retailer to slide into voluntary administration, putting nearly 500 jobs at risk as Australia’s retail sector continues to struggle with cash-strapped shoppers and online-only competitors.
The collapse comes not long after that of the upmarket department store David Jones and premium womenswear brands Cue and Veronika Maine, underscoring the mounting toll of tough economic conditions on established retailers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: General Pants Co enters voluntary administration, putting hundreds of jobs at risk

articles.author: Cait Kelly
articles.description:
Sports sections of British newspapers deliver their take on the unfolding Cricket Australia sandpaper saga 
The sports sections of the UK’s major mastheads are relishing the never-ending crisis engulfing Australian cricketing, after a key player in the ball tampering controversy, Cameron Bancroft, alleged everyone on the team knew about the 2018 plot.
Bancroft’s allegation came five days after a lengthy media conference by the current Australia Test captain, Pat Cummins, during which he denied that everyone on the team was in on the sandpaper plan. Cummins was responding to the allegation first aired in teammate Usman Khawaja’s biography, that actually, everyone did know about the sandpaper Bancroft was later caught holding.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Shame old Aussies’ to ‘fresh chaos’: what the UK papers say about Bancroft’s explosive ball tampering claims

articles.author: Sarah Johnson
articles.description:
Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds
One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.
In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo, Maanvi Singh, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed. 

Follow our live coverage of the Asia-Pacific economic cooperation summit

Sign up for US breaking News email

Linked to that, the White House held a briefing call with several reporters today about the wave of tech outages affecting several industries. CNN reported that officials said the administration underscored that what has happened is not as a result of cyber-attacks but due to the “hardening and upgrading of our systems”, including “systems being patched, hardware being applied”.
Per CNN, an official added: “It’s good the American people are focused on the need to upgrade our legacy systems.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump downplays US outages and Nvidia security concerns in remarks before China summit – as it happened

articles.author: Lucy Campbell and Robert Mackey
articles.description:
Musk, who aligned with Trump and was frequent White House guest, says he feels ‘pretty foolish’ about record midterm spending
Elon Musk denied being Maga on Wednesday, despite aligning himself intensely with Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again movement since 2024.
“I’m not Maga,” the world’s richest person told the New York Times Dealbook summit, which he attended via video call from China, where he is one of several US business leaders who have accompanied Trump on his trip to Asia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Elon Musk claims ‘I’m not Maga’ and says he regrets vast sums to back Republicans

articles.author: Lois Beckett
articles.description:
Storm expected to move into southern California, with LA residents warned of potential evacuation orders
Heavy rain pounded California’s Bay area, with record rainfall in downtown San Francisco and flooding and power outages across the region, as an “atmospheric river” arrived on Wednesday and dumped precipitation across the state.
The storm was expected to move into southern California on Wednesday night and Thursday, with Los Angeles warning residents in mudslide-prone areas of potential evacuation orders to come. Southern Californians were also warned of potential coastal flooding, heavy surf, wave damage to coastal piers and parking lots and beach sand erosion. Heavy snow warnings were issued for higher elevations of the Sierra Mountains, including in the Greater Lake Tahoe area.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Record-breaking rain lashes California’s Bay area as ‘atmospheric river’ arrives

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Bayesian, which sank off Sicily killing seven including tech tycoon, had not been fully assessed, say investigators
The superyacht Bayesian, which sank in a storm off Sicily killing seven people including the tech tycoon Mike Lynch and his teenage daughter, was vulnerable to knockdown but crew were not aware as it had never been assessed at anchor with its sails down, the final report from the UK’s Marine Accident Investigations Branch (MAIB) has said.
The 56-metre (184ft) vessel was anchored near the fishing port of Porticello when it sank during a violent storm shortly before dawn on 19 August 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mike Lynch’s superyacht had unidentified vulnerability to high winds, report finds

articles.author: Staff and agencies
articles.description:
Assessment of damage is underway, days after two attacks that destroyed road section of key bridge across Kerch strait linking annexed peninsula to Russia
A key bridge connecting annexed Crimea to Russia has been attacked again, a Russian-appointed regional governor has said, two days after Ukrainian strikes caused serious damage to it.
“Following a new attack on the Crimean Bridge, traffic has been temporarily halted. All relevant services are on site and at work. An assessment of the damage is under way,” Sergei Aksyonov, the Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea, wrote on Telegram. The Russian transport ministry said on Thursday that no one was wounded in the attack and that train services across it had been halted.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Crimea bridge has been attacked again, says Russian-installed governor

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo in Jerusalem
articles.description:
First incursion across boundary since ceasefire deal comes as Eisenkot seeks to form government without Netanyahu
The Israeli military crossed into Hamas-controlled central Gaza on Wednesday in its first ground operation across the “yellow line” boundary since a fragile ceasefire was agreed last October, forcing dozens of displaced Palestinians to flee their tents.
Israeli tanks rolled along the Salah al-Din road, Gaza’s main north-south route, a day after the US-backed Board of Peace, a body overseeing the ceasefire, accused Israel and Hamas of failing to honour their commitments to end hostilities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israeli tanks cross ‘yellow line’ boundary into Hamas-controlled central Gaza

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
articles.description:
Von der Leyen says she wants to give Kyiv ‘strong hand’ in talks and is confident all 27 member states will back idea 
The EU executive has proposed a €45bn (£37.5bn) loan for Ukraine to help with a looming cash crisis and reinforce its defences, as Russia’s relentless bombardment continues.
Announcing the plan to lend Kyiv the money in 2027, the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, said: “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table. And Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU proposes €45bn loan for Ukraine to avert cash crisis and boost defences

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse
A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse.
Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Florida pastor found guilty over 2021 assassination of Haitian president

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Housing minister hails ‘historic moment’ as he publishes bill to eventually ban almost all new leasehold properties
Leaseholders in England and Wales will have their ground rent capped in 2028, the housing minister has said as he publishes a bill that will eventually ban virtually all new leasehold properties.
Matthew Pennycook will introduce the government’s leasehold reform bill on Thursday, including measures to cap charges, end the sale of new leasehold flats and make it easier to extend and buy out leases.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Leaseholders in England and Wales to have ground rent capped in 2028

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The autonomous driving company suspended driverless taxi rides on US highways days after California banned the vehicles on its own freeways
Waymo has stopped offering driverless taxi rides on freeways across the US indefinitely. The Alphabet subsidiary pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after California banned them from freeways in response to recent traffic incidents.
Waymo had allowed riders to hail its robotaxis for freeway rides in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin. The California-based company offers rides on city streets in many other areas, including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver. Those rides remain unaffected by suspended freeway service.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Waymo pulls driverless taxis from freeways across the US after California ban

articles.author: Tom Phillips Latin America correspondent
articles.description:
Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago
Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.
Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hegseth uses Venezuela visit to boast of Maduro’s capture by US military

articles.author: Pippa Crerar, Lisa O’Carroll and Jessica Elgot
articles.description:
Diplomats say piecemeal approach of resets is coming to an end and Europe wants clarity on whether Britain wants to reverse its exit
The EU will shut the door to discussions with Andy Burnham about the UK’s longer-term relationship with the bloc until the government has decided whether it wants to proceed with reversing Brexit, diplomats have said.
European capitals are also warning they have reached the end of the line for piecemeal “reset” summits with the UK and want the prime minister to focus on his next steps domestically before they proceed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU ‘to close door’ to talks on long-term UK ties until Burnham has decided on Brexit

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
No 10 is confident the PM can make the case for closer EU ties, while others worry about leaving the campaign solely in his hands
The launch of a pro-Brexit campaign was one of the few genuine surprises this week in Westminster, even if the arguments were straight out of a familiar playbook.
The video launched on X over the weekend, with scenes of riots in France, champagne flowing in Brussels, and European politicians saying how desperate they were for Britain’s cash.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The leave campaign has been resurrected, so how should Burnham respond?

articles.author: Tom Ambrose (now); Taz Ali and Kate Lamb (earlier)
articles.description:
This blog is now closed, you can read more on this story here
Yalta became a byword for betrayal. Will Trump, Xi and Putin enact another carve-up?
That is the question the Guardian’s diplomatic correspondent Patrick Wintour seeks to address in his piece about the expected, Putin, Trump and Xi, meeting at Apec on Thursday.
It is a truism in diplomacy that if you are not around the table, the risk is that you, or your values, are on the menu and about to be carved up. Many excluded from the summit in Shenzhen, principally Ukraine but also eastern Europe and Baltic countries, Taiwan and even Iran, have reason to be nervous that their sponsors might abandon them in a complex geopolitical trade-off that Putin envisions, and Trump seems to endorse.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Apec summit as it happened: Xi welcomes Trump on China visit as Putin claims Europe in ‘humiliating decline’

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Attorney general says E1 settlement decision should not be taken by caretaker government led by Netanyahu
Israel has postponed issuing contracts for the construction of a large settlement on the West Bank seen as likely to render a two-state solution unviable, days after the UK imposed sanctions against building firms operating in the area.
Israeli diplomats insisted the move was not in response to the measures from Downing Street. Gali Baharav-Miara, the attorney general, said any decision on settlement expansion should not be taken by the caretaker government led by Benjamin Netanyahu but by whatever new administration was formed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israel delays building contracts for West Bank settlement after UK sanctions

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza
Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.
The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
articles.description:
Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans
The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.
The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt

articles.author: Raphael Rashid in Seoul
articles.description:
South Korea has been gripped by revelations of AI-aided cheating, just days before more than half a million students are to sit high-stakes entrance exams
The integrity of South Korea’s career-defining university entrance exam has been thrown into doubt after the top scorer in a recent professional exam admitted using a concealed camera and AI to cheat.
On Thursday, more than half a million people, mostly school students, are due to sit the exam, known as the suneung, at 1,312 centres across the country. The exam runs for a gruelling eight hours over a single day and determines which university a candidate can attend and, in turn, their future prospects.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: South Korea’s high-stakes university exams upended by AI cheating scandal

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Asif Merchant, allegedly linked to Iran, found by court to have sought retribution over Qassem Suleimani death
A Pakistani man was sentenced to more than 27 years in prison on Tuesday for plotting to assassinate Donald Trump in retaliation for the US killing of Revolutionary Guards commander Qassem Suleimani, the Department of Justice said.
Asif Merchant, who had alleged ties to Iran, sought to hire a hitman to assassinate a politician or a government official in the United States, a Brooklyn court found.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years in US prison over Trump murder plot

articles.author: Associated Press in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Knesset’s appointment of Matan Kahana marks step towards reversing policies of outgoing government
The Israeli parliament elected a new speaker on Tuesday, a key step toward rolling back policies passed by the outgoing government led by the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.
The new speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Netanyahu.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Israeli parliament elects new speaker backed by Netanyahu’s opponents

articles.author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent
articles.description:
St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free access
The decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned.
On Friday, Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the twin-island Caribbean nation, announced he would wind down the citizenship-by-investment (CBI) programme, after the European Union threatened to end visa-free access for St Kitts and Nevis.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Caribbean nations fear economic impact of shuttering citizenship program after EU threats

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Indigenous Awá people of Amazon make contact with villagers and accept food to take back to territory
About 20 Indigenous people emerged from isolation in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, several organizations reported on Tuesday, raising the alarm about increased invasions into the tribe’s territory.
According to the NGO Survival International, members of the Awá people, who live in voluntary isolation, arrived on Monday in a village and made contact with a government team in a “historic encounter”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Isolated Brazilian tribe emerges amid alarm over threats to group’s way of life

articles.author: Cecilia Nowell
articles.description:
Child reunited with family after he was detained by immigration agents in San Diego and transferred to Texas
An eight-year-old Haitian boy who was put into restraints and detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November and transferred to a facility in Texas has been reunited with his family in California.
Representative Juan Vargas shared a photograph of the boy and his family in a social media post on Monda, writing: “11 days ago, an 8-year-old in San Diego was taken into federal custody during an immigration check-in. He was separated from his loved ones and held in a facility in Texas. Today, he’s finally home.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Eight-year-old Haitian boy returns home after release from ICE custody

articles.author: Lorenzo Tondo and Sufian Taha in Jerusalem
articles.description:
Bullet hit 72-year-old Fadha Wadha in head outside her home in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, in the West Bank, say residents
A 72-year-old Palestinian woman has been shot dead in an overnight attack by Israeli settlers in a village near Jericho where settlers have recently moved in after taking over several Palestinian homes.
Fadha Wadha was standing outside her home in al-Duyuk al-Tahta in the occupied West Bank when she was struck in the head by a bullet as Israeli settlers fired towards Palestinian houses, according to testimonies from residents. Several other Palestinians, including her son, were wounded by gunfire.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Palestinian woman shot dead by Israeli settlers near Jericho, witnesses say

articles.author: Cris Seda Chabrier
articles.description:
High-stakes hearing comes in wake of resignation from Nvidia after alleged affair with suspected Chinese spy
Nvidia’s former CEO Jensen Huang will testify before several congressional committees on 1 December, setting the stage for a high-stakes hearing in the wake of his resignation following an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
Tim Teter, Nvidia’s general counsel, has also agreed to appear for a closed-door transcribed interview the following day, 2 December.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jensen Huang to testify before Congress on ‘potential breach of national security’

articles.author: Rebecca Bailey in Shenzhen
articles.description:
Host city offers showcase of China’s rise into a confident and innovative power central to global economy
In a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping, is basking in its neon glow.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hi-tech Shenzhen takes centre stage as Xi sends ‘Chinamaxxing’ message at Apec summit

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
As tourism booms, three experienced female travellers give their take on how to make the most of travelling here
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
The 13th-century Persian scholar Zakariyya al-Qazwini never travelled to India. But he catalogued it in his famous work The Wonders of Creation and Rarities of Existence, which drew on accounts of a distant land filled with “rarities par excellence”. For al-Qazwini, as Helen Pfeifer writes in the London Review of Books, wonder was not an emotion but an intellectual method of making sense of the world and acquiring knowledge.
India has long occupied such a space in the global imagination, as a land of extraordinary riches; spirituality, customs, chaos and contradictions. This has shaped how the country is perceived from afar, but it can often flatten its complexities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India has been named a ‘destination of the year’ for 2027 – here are insiders’ tips on travelling beyond the tropes

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
articles.description:
Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’
Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.
The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda

articles.author: Guardian sport
articles.description:
Suspect named as Greene Da’monte Khiree

Drug smuggling carries life sentence in Nigeria

An American basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria for allegedly attempting to smuggle 33.95kg (75lb) of marijuana into the country.
Nigeria’s National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said a 28-year-old player named as Greene Da’monte Khiree from the state of Georgia was arrested at Lagos’s main airport last Wednesday after he arrived on a flight from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US basketball player arrested with 75lb of marijuana at Nigerian airport, say authorities

articles.author: Imran Lodhi, as told to Morgan Krakow
articles.description:
When the floods hit Pakistan he went out to help. Then the water reached his own family. This is Imran Lodhi’s story
Location: Dera Ghazi Khan, Pakistan
Disaster: Pakistan intense monsoon rainfall
Imran Lodhi is a university lecturer with a doctorate in climate change and sustainable development. The 41-year-old was living in Dera Ghazi Khan, a city in south-western Punjab, when floods devastated provinces across Pakistan. Climate change made the monsoon rainfall that caused the floods more intense.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I saw a picture of a two-year-old girl buried in mud. I knew we had to do something’ – This is climate breakdown

articles.author: Oliver Holmes and Kaamil Ahmed
articles.description:
International court of justice has never before found a state guilty of genocide, and ruling will have implications for case against Israel
The world’s top court will deliver a judgment this week on whether Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, in a landmark case that will set a critical 21st-century benchmark for the gravest of all international crimes.
The closely watched judgment could become one of the most significant moments in international law since the end of the second world war.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: World’s top court to rule if Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Aakash Hassan in Delhi
articles.description:
Former prime minister faces death penalty upon return after being sentenced in absentia over deaths in 2024 uprising
Sheikh Hasina is “confident” she will return to Bangladesh in December, according to exiled members of her party, after the disgraced former prime minister applied for a new passport this week.
Hasina has been living in self-imposed exile since August 2024 when she was toppled from power by a mass uprising against her authoritarian rule. She crossed the border to India, where she has since been allowed to live freely in Delhi.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Disgraced former leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh from exile

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
From the assassinations of her husband and mother-in-law to press stonewalling under Modi, Belonging offers an insider’s account of India’s political evolution
• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Few love stories have been as closely entwined with a nation’s history as that of Sonia and Rajiv Gandhi. The former’s much-awaited political memoir, Belonging, offers a strikingly candid account of her journey from a small town in Italy to the highest echelons of power in India – all for love, she says.
The veteran Congress party leader has been fiercely protective of her personal world. In Belonging, she opens up for the first time about the extraordinary twists and turns of a life that has largely unfolded in full public view. (The Guardian’s Hannah Ellis-Petersen has a rare in-person interview with Gandhi, and you can read an excerpt from the book here.)
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Grenades, grief and a deepening political divide: five takeaways from Sonia Gandhi’s new memoir

articles.author: Presented by Ian Sample, with Jessica Glenza, produced by Ellie Sans, sound design by Joel Cox; the executive producer was Ellie Bury
articles.description:
This week the US lost its measles elimination status, an official recognition that the infectious disease is endemic in the country after being eliminated for 26 years. To find out what this means in practical terms for citizens, Ian Sample hears from the Guardian US health reporter Jessica Glenza. She explains why it comes at an already difficult time for the health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, and his Make America Healthy Again movement, and what newly elected Democrats will be focusing on when it comes to health
Clips: CBS, NBC, CBC
US loses measles elimination status amid worst outbreak since 1991
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Could measles and midterms bring down Maha? – podcast

articles.author: Uwa Ede-Osifo, Maanvi Singh, Shrai Popat, Lucy Campbell and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed. 

Follow our live coverage of the Asia-Pacific economic cooperation summit

Sign up for US breaking News email

Linked to that, the White House held a briefing call with several reporters today about the wave of tech outages affecting several industries. CNN reported that officials said the administration underscored that what has happened is not as a result of cyber-attacks but due to the “hardening and upgrading of our systems”, including “systems being patched, hardware being applied”.
Per CNN, an official added: “It’s good the American people are focused on the need to upgrade our legacy systems.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump downplays US outages and Nvidia security concerns in remarks before China summit – as it happened

articles.author: Lucy Campbell and Robert Mackey
articles.description:
Musk, who aligned with Trump and was frequent White House guest, says he feels ‘pretty foolish’ about record midterm spending
Elon Musk denied being Maga on Wednesday, despite aligning himself intensely with Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again movement since 2024.
“I’m not Maga,” the world’s richest person told the New York Times Dealbook summit, which he attended via video call from China, where he is one of several US business leaders who have accompanied Trump on his trip to Asia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Elon Musk claims ‘I’m not Maga’ and says he regrets vast sums to back Republicans

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon and Shrai Popat in Washington
articles.description:
Robert Garcia plans searches into Trump family finances, alleged DHS misconduct and handling of Epstein files
The incoming Democratic chair of the powerful oversight committee in the House of Representatives has ordered a dozen relatives and allies of Donald Trump to preserve records before investigations he plans to open.
Robert Garcia sent 12 letters on Wednesday to prominent figures in the US president’s orbit, including his sons Donald Jr and Eric; son-in-law Jared Kushner; the vice-president, JD Vance; and the attorney general, Todd Blanche.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump family and allies told to preserve records as Democrats prepare sweeping investigations

articles.author: Timothy Pratt
articles.description:
DoJ cites three examples of alterations from English into Spanish for James ‘Fergie’ Chambers after Guardian report
US authorities have admitted altering the translation of an extradition request for James “Fergie” Chambers from English into Spanish, attributing violent and illegal actions to the wealthy activist and philanthropist that were not in the original.
Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money-laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US admits ‘substantial’ change to extradition request translation for leftist activist

articles.description:
The homeland security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, defended his decision to take a government plane to attend a football game between Louisiana State University and the University of Texas on Saturday, while thousands of flights had been canceled and airspace was closed during the Federal Aviation Administration's nationwide ground stop over the weekend
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mullin defends taking government plane to college football game amid nationwide grounding – video

articles.author: Norman Solomon
articles.description:
The likely next House speaker has a record of defending corporate interests. His fellow Democrats must fight for Medicare for All and the abolition of ICE
On Wednesday, Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries to be the next House speaker when they take control of Congress. For progressives, that will mean dealing with a powerful leader who has a record of hostility toward the left.
“There will never be a moment where I bend the knee to hard-left democratic socialism,” Jeffries vowed five years ago.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Can progressives push Hakeem Jeffries to the left? | Norman Solomon

articles.author: Sanya Mansoor
articles.description:
Cair-Florida is suing state officials after designation meant it had to shut its doors to victims of harassment and discrimination
Omar Soboh, a student at the University of Florida, was organizing a campus panel about Islamophobia when he found out one of the groups being represented had suddenly been blacklisted by the state. Under a new process, Florida had designated the Council on American-Islamic Relations (Cair), the nation’s largest Muslim civil rights group, a domestic terrorist organization. The university’s Arab Students’ Association decided to cancel the event, and Soboh, who is Palestinian American, was disheartened.
“Our existence itself is political,” he said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: This Muslim civil rights group defended pro-Palestine protesters. Then Florida labeled it a terrorist organization

articles.author: Andrew Lawrence
articles.description:
After refusing to obey the president’s Lake Ontario order, MapQuest briefly rose to No 1 in navigation apps. It’s now a tool in the US anti-surveillance movement
I am among the legion of former PC desk occupants with warm memories of MapQuest, the Y2K-era travel website that kept millennial drivers on course with sheaves of printed-out directions – a quantum leap over the ungainly glovebox map. But I assumed it had long since gone the way of AIM and Skype, its manual turn-by-turn guidance made obsolete by big tech.
Proof of life came in January 2025, when Donald Trump issued an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America – a change Apple Maps and Google Maps promptly adopted, while MapQuest … did nothing. Not only had it never signed off, MapQuest was reinventing itself as a plucky oppositional hero, the app most likely to uphold your geographical beliefs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Annoying Trump and dodging Flock: inside MapQuest’s contrarian comeback

articles.author: Alice Speri
articles.description:
With its policy priorities more mainstream than ever, the left is directing its momentum toward 2028
A week after the US midterm elections swept an unprecedented number of leftists into office across the country, about 600 people joined a Zoom call. The goal: to convince Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president.
On the call, organizers from Ready for AOC, a new group of progressive and labor organizers, wasted little time celebrating the Democrats’ electoral sweep. “People all over the country are ready for a much different and much better future,” said Genevieve Rand, an organizer with the group. “We are more ready than we have ever been.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fresh off recent wins, the left has a new goal: get AOC to run for president

articles.description:
Hung Cao, the acting US navy secretary, who faced lawmakers to be confirmed as the permanent top official, said during his confirmation hearing that the eight suicide attempts on board the USS Abraham Lincoln – which returned last month from a record-breaking deployment rife with mental health crises and concerns about living conditions – were actually “suicide mitigations”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Acting US navy secretary refers to eight suicide attempts as 'suicide mitigations' – video

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
Now the vice-president’s luck is turning, he seems reluctant to commit himself to the next presidential race – and I, for one, hate to see it
How do you think history will remember JD Vance? As the first vice-president to spark a vigorous debate about their eyeliner routine? As one of the last public figures to see Pope Francis alive? As the only politician in US history to have been the subject of a rumour about sexual relations with a couch (even though it was unfounded)?
I have no idea. But it seems increasingly unlikely he will be remembered as the 48th president of the US. After Maga’s midterm thrashing, Vance’s political future doesn’t look as bright as it used to. So much so that there has been a flurry of recent headlines debating whether or not Vance, once considered Donald Trump’s heir apparent, may slink away from a presidential run altogether.
Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? If you would like to submit a response of up to 300 words by email to be considered for publication in our letters section, please click here.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Should JD Vance run for president? I say go for it, habibi! | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Gabrielle Canon in Antalya
articles.description:
The 120-strong America Is All In group are trying to ensure that the US won’t remained sidelined at the climate talks for very much longer. Plus: wild oysters are back in Scotland and a super El Niño looms over Cop
• Don’t get Down to Earth delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
The final week of Cop31 is in full swing, with just four days left to set a broad range of climate commitments into concrete action. I am on the ground at this year’s UN annual climate summit, where thousands of world leaders, businesses, nonprofits and scientists have converged in Antalya, Turkey, and there’s a lot left to do as the clock ticks down.
“Nearly 200 countries are working through 165 mandates,” executive secretary Simon Stiell told reporters at the midpoint on Saturday, pushing for a swift move to the hardest issues and championing compromise. “Each country has a view,” he said. “Every country has a voice.”
European-made pesticides named in 1,605 poisoning reports in Brazil last year
AI models ‘weak and fallible’ on climate science, UN-backed study reports
‘I was home alone when the glacier collapsed. My mum called and told me to run’
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We are all in’: the Democrats trying to turn round the US’s reputation at Cop31

articles.author: Wajahat Ali
articles.description:
America’s future depends on progressive, anti-establishment fighters
Welcome back to How We Win, a Guardian opinion series with leading thinkers, offering bold ideas for America’s political future. Last week, Naomi Klein, Guardian US columnist, argued for taking on the billionaire class. Today’s edition was written by Wajahat Ali, editor of The Left Hook and co-host of The Democracy-ish Podcast.
Change is slow, and then, once in a while, all of a sudden.
The future of America depends on progressive, anti-establishment fighters to champion a politics of transformation.
Tax billionaires.
Medicare for All.
Abolish ICE and put forth an immigration reform policy that centers both humanity and security.
Call out Israel’s genocide and withhold money and weapons from foreign countries that commit war crimes with our resources.
A living wage.
Reject corporate Pac money and deliver campaign finance reform.
Combat climate change and move away from fossil fuels.
Expand and aggressively reform the supreme court, because without that, we get nothing.
Deliver accountability for “the Epstein class”, a transnational syndicate of powerful billionaires who commit crimes with impunity.
Never sacrifice or abandon any marginalized group in our pursuit of affordability and accountability.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Let’s take over the ossified Democratic party and deliver a modern New Deal

articles.author: Sidney Blumenthal
articles.description:
Horowitz, who swung from the far left to the far right, sought total political warfare against institutions and immigration 
Stephen Miller has risen to the top of the White House in the downdraft of Donald Trump’s abject defeat in the midterm elections. It is no irony to Trump that he has elevated Miller as his ideal bullying enforcer only after Trump’s own thorough repudiation. Appointing Miller is Trump’s denial that he is the worst thing he could possibly imagine: a loser.
Trump has no more time for adults in the room who might want to negotiate with the new powers-that-be in the Congress. He has searched his soul, as he explained in his interview on 60 Minutes, entertaining his wish to ascend to heaven.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How the rightwing operative David Horowitz shaped Stephen Miller | Sidney Blumenthal

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright with Chris Stein and Rachel Leingang, produced by Monica Espitia and Anabel Bacon, engineered by Ivan Kuraev , executive producer Rachel Humphreys
articles.description:
The blue wave has hit Washington, and with the flood of new Democratic lawmakers comes a debate over who should lead the party. On Monday, Maryland senator Chris Van Hollen said his campaign to unseat Chuck Schumer as Senate majority leader is gathering momentum. He has painted himself as the underdog candidate to Schumer, who has led Senate Democrats for nearly a decade. What does this leadership battle tell us about the kind of party Democrats want to be? Kai Wright speaks to the Guardian’s senior politics reporter Chris Stein about Van Hollen's chances, and hears from the Guardian's midwest political correspondent Rachel Leingang about why new senators in her region are having doubts about Schumer
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Can Chris Van Hollen really beat Chuck Schumer? – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Aisha Down ; produced by Hana Williams ; senior producer Angus Neale ; executive producer Zoe Hitch
articles.description:
Jensen Huang’s resignation from the AI chipmaker Nvidia has sent shockwaves through the global economy. Huang resigned after reported affairs with an Nvidia executive and a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. The fallout is not over yet, with criticism mounting over the apparent lack of action from the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick. Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s global technology reporter, Aisha Down
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why the Nvidia scandal is far from over - The Latest

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Modelling in draft of 10-year London plan threatens Sadiq Khan’s promises on improving air quality
Car use in London will rise by 10% over the next decade with cycling and walking falling as a proportion of trips, according to an official forecast by the city’s mayoralty, putting into doubt Sadiq Khan’s promises on air quality and the environment.
Based on projections in the draft version of the latest 10-year London plan, drawn up by the mayor’s office and Transport for London (TfL), road congestion from a growing population would slow buses down, while packed tube services might require stations to close regularly to ease numbers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Car use in London forecast to rise by 10% in next decade

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
UK central bank will want to avoid echoes of expensive US Federal Reserve revamp that led to Trump clash
Andrew Bailey may spend his days closely watching developments in the strait of Hormuz or US stock markets for signs of shocks to the global economy – but the Bank of England’s governor has a £160m problem brewing much closer to home.
A secretive major revamp of the Bank’s historic headquarters in the heart of London’s Square Mile presents a huge test of Bailey’s project management skills. The central bank, with its reputation staked on carefully counting the nation’s pennies, will be keen to avoid delays, budget-busting or any echoes of the expensive US Federal Reserve revamp that left his former peer Jerome Powell awkwardly clashing with Donald Trump on camera.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Grade I interiors, gold bars, cost fears: Bank of England faces headache over £160m revamp

articles.author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
articles.description:
Former minister, who was sentenced to prison in Bangladesh in her absence, says she was victim of ‘malicious prosecution’
The former minister Tulip Siddiq has said she is considering taking legal action against the former interim leader of Bangladesh over corruption allegations made by his administration led her to resign from the UK government last year.
The MP for Hampstead and Highgate, whose aunt Sheikh Hasina was put on trial in absentia over crimes against humanity during her 15 years as prime minister of Bangladesh, was accused of benefiting from the former regime by the authorities in the Bangladeshi capital, Dhaka.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tulip Siddiq says she is considering legal action against former Bangladesh leader

articles.author: Patrick Barkham
articles.description:
Scientists use lightweight tracker to map wading bird’s extraordinary migration from Norfolk to the Arctic and back
A bar-tailed godwit called Phil has completed a 6,800-mile journey from Norfolk to Siberia and back again, in the first mapping of the endurance feats of this long-distance migrant.
A wading bird not much larger than a pigeon, the bar-tailed godwit is known for making the longest recorded non-stop migratory flight of any bird, with populations that visit Britain spending summers breeding in the Arctic Circle before retreating to the unfrozen wetlands of Britain in winter.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Meet Phil, the bar-tailed godwit tracked on a 6,800-mile round trip to Siberia

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
About 2.6m adults are taking the drugs, fuelled by the regulator’s approval of the pill versions and a rise in male users
At least one person is taking weight-loss drugs in 8.5% of households in Great Britain, according to research, meaning there are more homes with GLP-1 users than those containing vegetarians and pescatarians combined.
About 2.6 million adults were using weight-loss medication in August, a rise of about 700,000 people since February, according to a survey by Worldpanel by Numerator.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Weight-loss drugs used in nearly one in 10 homes in Great Britain, study finds

articles.author: Presented by Annie Kelly with Jessica Elgot and David McAllister; produced by Eleanor Biggs, Alex Atack, Harriet Mogie and Brian McNamara; executive producer Sami Kent
articles.description:
Deputy political editor Jessica Elgot and influential MEP David McAllister on the prospect of the UK rejoining the European Union, before Friday’s UK-EU summit
On Friday, Andy Burnham will be in Brussels, to sign off a series of new deals between the UK and the EU.
The prime minister claims the deals – covering areas from food to youth mobility to carbon emissions – will boost UK GDP by £17bn.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brejoin? Is Andy Burnham going to reverse Brexit? – podcast

articles.author: Caroline Davies
articles.description:
Bayesian, which sank off Sicily killing seven including tech tycoon, had not been fully assessed, say investigators
The superyacht Bayesian, which sank in a storm off Sicily killing seven people including the tech tycoon Mike Lynch and his teenage daughter, was vulnerable to knockdown but crew were not aware as it had never been assessed at anchor with its sails down, the final report from the UK’s Marine Accident Investigations Branch (MAIB) has said.
The 56-metre (184ft) vessel was anchored near the fishing port of Porticello when it sank during a violent storm shortly before dawn on 19 August 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mike Lynch’s superyacht had unidentified vulnerability to high winds, report finds

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Housing minister hails ‘historic moment’ as he publishes bill to eventually ban almost all new leasehold properties
Leaseholders in England and Wales will have their ground rent capped in 2028, the housing minister has said as he publishes a bill that will eventually ban virtually all new leasehold properties.
Matthew Pennycook will introduce the government’s leasehold reform bill on Thursday, including measures to cap charges, end the sale of new leasehold flats and make it easier to extend and buy out leases.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Leaseholders in England and Wales to have ground rent capped in 2028

articles.author: Neha Gohil
articles.description:
Raise the Colours activist Billy Allison, 36, killed man in ‘completely unprovoked and unjustified’ attack, say police
A member of anti-migrant group Raise the Colours has been found guilty of murdering a man in a “completely unprovoked and unjustified” attack.
Billy Allison, 36, delivered a “very, very hard” punch with the “stance and skill of an experienced fighter” which killed 44-year-old Matthew O’Gara while he was on a night out in Lichfield on 24 May.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Member of anti-migrant group found guilty of Staffordshire murder

articles.author: Neha Gohil Midlands correspondent
articles.description:
High court judge issues order against Raise the Colours over flags on council-owned street furniture
The campaign group Raise the Colours has been temporarily banned from placing union jacks on lamp-posts and roundabouts in Birmingham after a legal challenge by the local council.
The high court judge Emma Kelly granted an interim injunction banning the placing of all flags on council-owned street furniture without prior permission in a judgment issued on Wednesday, Birmingham city council said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Birmingham council granted interim ban on union jacks on lamp-posts

articles.author: Vikram Dodd Police and crime correspondent
articles.description:
Home secretary says ‘routine two-tier policing’ does not exist, but public trust in impartial law enforcement must be restored
Shabana Mahmood has backed a ban on police officers marching in pride events in uniform as she said there had been a “few examples” of two-tier policing.
Although she said there was no systematic or routine two-tier policing, the home secretary said “a new impartiality standard” was necessary to reverse the fall in the public’s faith in law enforcement.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Shabana Mahmood backs ban on police marching in pride events in uniform

articles.author: Pippa Crerar, Lisa O’Carroll and Jessica Elgot
articles.description:
Diplomats say piecemeal approach of resets is coming to an end and Europe wants clarity on whether Britain wants to reverse its exit
The EU will shut the door to discussions with Andy Burnham about the UK’s longer-term relationship with the bloc until the government has decided whether it wants to proceed with reversing Brexit, diplomats have said.
European capitals are also warning they have reached the end of the line for piecemeal “reset” summits with the UK and want the prime minister to focus on his next steps domestically before they proceed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU ‘to close door’ to talks on long-term UK ties until Burnham has decided on Brexit

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
No 10 is confident the PM can make the case for closer EU ties, while others worry about leaving the campaign solely in his hands
The launch of a pro-Brexit campaign was one of the few genuine surprises this week in Westminster, even if the arguments were straight out of a familiar playbook.
The video launched on X over the weekend, with scenes of riots in France, champagne flowing in Brussels, and European politicians saying how desperate they were for Britain’s cash.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The leave campaign has been resurrected, so how should Burnham respond?

articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
articles.description:
Health secretary said programme would help about 566,000 vulnerable people in England by April
More than half a million of the most vulnerable people in England will be offered help from joint NHS and social care teams that will pave the way for the promised national care service, Yvette Cooper has announced.
Elderly people, care home residents, those with dementia and people near the end of their lives will receive assistance from the new programme.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Neighbourhood support teams’ to pave way for national care service, Cooper announces

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah ,  Kiran Stacey and Peter Walker
articles.description:
PM hints he is open to suggestion in Milburn report to lower NICs contributions paid by companies for under-25s

Who are the Neets? UK youth job crisis in five charts

UK firms: what is stopping you hiring young people?

Andy Burnham has said he would consider cuts to national insurance for young people “very carefully”.
The prime minister also believes his proposed changes to welfare are a “very different proposition” from those of his predecessor, Keir Starmer, and the former chancellor Rachel Reeves in the last government.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham considering cuts to national insurance to create more youth jobs

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
articles.description:
Leaked text of 72-paragraph second draft shows agreement has largely been reached before expected signoff on Friday
The UK-EU “relationship reset” agreement, which began in earnest under Keir Starmer, is expected to be signed off by Andy Burnham in Brussels on Friday.
A leaked text of the second draft shows an agreement has largely been reached with some outstanding points.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cheese, pet passports and youth mobility: what’s in the UK-EU ‘relationship reset’ draft?

articles.author: Ian Sample Science editor
articles.description:
Scientists tell Commons exposure to colibactin in early life is potential driver of early-onset colorectal cancer
Exposure to a bacterial toxin in early life has emerged as a leading suspect in the rise of bowel cancer among those under 50, MPs have heard.
Cases of early-onset bowel cancer have doubled in many countries in the past two decades, and while rising obesity and a fall in physical activity are contributors, researchers believe other factors must also be involved.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bacterial toxin produced by E coli leading suspect in rise in bowel cancer among under-50s

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
This blog is now closed
In her speech today, Shabana Mahmood, the home secretary, will also announce plans for a new fast-stream police leadership programme for up to 200 recruits a year. Vikram Dodd has the details.
The Conservatives and Reform UK do not seem very impressed by Shabana Mahmood’s proposal to meet their concerns about two-tier policing.
If you don’t want two-tier justice, stop legislating for it.
Stop training people for it.
Last year the Home Office believed claims of “two-tier” policing were “far-right”. Will they now apologise?
Even in her statement Mahmood still can’t bring herself to say it’s wrong.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: PM urges Badenoch to withdraw ‘crass’ defence of disability cuts on grounds ‘amputees run marathons’ – as it happened

articles.author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
articles.description:
Trust apologises after findings on treatment of 20 brain tumour patients under oncologist who retired in 2023
Cancer patients were severely harmed after being given years of unnecessary chemotherapy treatment by an NHS trust, a report has found.
Some people were misdiagnosed and given inappropriate courses of treatment, while others were incorrectly told that if they stopped chemotherapy they would die, according to a Royal College of Physicians (RCP) report.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cancer patients at NHS trust harmed by years of unnecessary chemotherapy, report finds

articles.author: Hilary Osborne Consumer and money editor
articles.description:
It is possible to switch to a better tariff and save money despite the forecast rise next year

Average energy bill in Great Britain predicted to rise to £2,166

The energy price cap in Great Britain looks likely to go up by 26% in January. But your bills might not have to rise by the same amount. If you are paying a tariff that matches the price cap you could save by switching to something lower. And if you do it now, you could make a substantial saving.
Providers are offering fixed tariffs that work out up to £407 below the estimated price cap, according to price comparison website uSwitch. It’s worth noting that it’s the price of the energy you use that is fixed, not your bill – so you will still be charged according to what you use.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Energy price cap rise: how to switch providers

articles.author: David Conn and Felicity Lawrence
articles.description:
Exclusive: Jury was never told that Prof Peter Hindmarsh was barred from practising over concerns for patients’ safety
A senior doctor whose evidence helped to convict Lucy Letby and who was held up by prosecutors as a pre-eminent expert was barred from treating patients during the trial over fears he posed a risk to their safety.
Prof Peter Hindmarsh, a specialist in hormones in children, was crucial to the crown’s argument that the British nurse had poisoned children by injecting insulin into fluid bags. But a Guardian investigation can reveal he was excluded from clinical practice in March 2023, five months before the end of the trial, by his employer, University College London hospitals trust (UCLH). Jurors were never told.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Doctor whose evidence helped to convict Lucy Letby was barred from treating patients during trial

articles.author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
articles.description:
Increase in October piles pressure on households as Iran war pushes up oil cost and rattles global economy

Energy bills in Great Britain forecast to rise by 26% to £2,166 from January

Inflation in the UK rose to 3.6% in October after petrol prices increased and diesel hit a record high amid the fallout from the war in the Middle East.
Figures from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) show the headline rate of inflation as measured by the consumer prices index rose from 3.5% in September and was in line with City economists’ forecasts.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK inflation rises to 3.6% after petrol and diesel prices hit record high

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
articles.description:
Government under pressure to help households as increase would add £443 to average annual dual-fuel bill

Energy price cap rise: how to switch providers

Tell us: are you shopping around for a better deal?

UK inflation rises to 3.6%

Energy bills across Great Britain are predicted to reach £2,166 a year for the typical household from January as the impact of the Middle East conflict piles pressure on the government to offer more support to hard-hit households.
The government’s cap on gas and electricity prices is likely to rise by 26% early next year, equivalent to adding £443 to the average annual dual-fuel bill, in one of the biggest quarterly price rises on record, according to the leading forecaster Cornwall Insight.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Energy bills in Great Britain forecast to rise by 26% to £2,166 from January

articles.author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
articles.description:
Meaning and use of word has become more important in age of AI chatbot, says dictionary
In a world where the line between people and machines is more blurred than ever, Cambridge dictionary has sided with natural intelligence for its word of the year: human.
Breakthroughs in artificial intelligence – led by the arrival of ChatGPT three years ago – have made the question of what it means to be human as vexed as ever, but the dictionary has drawn a firm line with its choice of the word of 2026, defining “human” as “having the qualities, faults, and feelings that people have, as opposed to gods, animals, or machines”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Human’ wins Cambridge dictionary’s word of the year

articles.author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal; produced by George McDonagh, Ivor Manley , Harriet Mogie and Rudi Zygadlo; executive producer Eli Block
articles.description:
There are about a million young people across the country not in employment, education or training. Could Alan Milburn’s landmark report help change that? Richard Partington reports
The UK has one of the worst rates in Europe when it comes to youth unemployment. From the savage cuts to youth services during austerity, to the impacts of the pandemic and now the threat of AI to entry level jobs, young people across the country are feeling that the social contract is broken.
But now Alan Milburn, the 68-year-old New Labour veteran, has published a radical review urging the government to spend billions on a new deal for young people.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Can Labour end the youth unemployment crisis? – podcast

articles.author: Jasper Jolly, Jillian Ambrose and Kiran Stacey
articles.description:
Analysts say mooted move to let more petrol and diesel vehicles be sold would wreck plan to reach net zero by 2050

Weakening the UK’s electric car sales rules would probably cause the government to miss legally binding climate targets, according to advisers tracking Britain’s progress to net zero.
The analysis by the Climate Change Committee (CCC) suggests the policy would blow a hole in the plan for achieving net zero carbon emissions by 2050 – prompting concerns that Andy Burnham’s government will have to slash the UK’s carbon emissions reduction targets, known as the carbon budgets.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK will miss climate targets if it weakens EV sales rules, advisers warn

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
articles.description:
CBI says restrictions on cross-Channel work trips are hindering investment and trade between UK and Europe
Business chiefs have called on the UK government and the European Commission to urgently ease Brexit restrictions on business travel for cross-Channel work trips.
A group representing industry bosses said it wants commitments from Andy Burnham and European political leaders that the restrictions will be one of the priorities in 2027 for furthering ties between the two sides, after a summit in Brussels this week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brexit work travel rules need urgent improvement, say UK business leaders

articles.author: Sally Weale Education correspondent
articles.description:
Vice-chancellor halts proposed relocation from Stratford-upon-Avon but offers no guarantees over future
The University of Birmingham has paused plans to move its much-loved Shakespeare Institute from Stratford-upon-Avon to its city campus after an outcry from scholars, actors and enthusiasts around the world.
Prof Adam Tickell, the university’s vice-chancellor and principal, issued a statement on Tuesday evening saying proposals to relocate the institute and its renowned 60,000-volume library to the university’s Edgbaston campus would be put on hold while its future was explored.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: University of Birmingham pauses plans to move Shakespeare Institute after outcry

articles.author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
articles.description:
He lays out sweeping aims and finer details for how to fix the Neets crisis – and is obsessive about welfare

Neet ideas: what’s in Milburn’s report?

It is not clear if too many people were expecting Everything Everywhere All at Once, but that is what Alan Milburn has delivered. From a Welfare State to a Working State is almost absurdly ambitious. The terms of reference said something about the drivers of youth labour markets. We got a blueprint for how to fix everything and everyone.
What Keir Starmer, who commissioned it, had in mind, we’ll never know, but Milburn has taken up with gusto Andy Burnham’s general invocation to think boldly and rewire the state. Yes, it’s about training and jobs, but it’s also about pulling apart the NHS, giving schools and colleges an MOT, and once again, blowing up old-fashioned social security.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Milburn’s absurdly ambitious report offers blueprint for fixing everything and everyone

articles.author: Jonathan Watts
articles.description:
We look at what is happening over the Arctic and what it might mean for winter weather in the northern hemisphere
The polar vortex has flipped direction, signalling the earliest “major sudden stratospheric warming” ever observed. We examine how it is likely to affect you and whether it will bring snow.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What is the polar vortex, why has it flipped and will it bring snow?

articles.description:
Alan Milburn has warned that the UK is at risk of losing a generation of young people without radical reform to tackle youth unemployment. Speaking at the launch of his report at Google's London headquarters, the former health secretary insisted 'half measures will not do' as he outlined proposals to get more young people into work that could save the government £200m a year


Alan Milburn says his plan to get young people into work will save only £200m a year

UK politics live – latest updates

Neet ideas: what’s in Milburn’s report?

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alan Milburn says 'Great British promise' to young people is being broken – video

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
Agreement secured by Equity union gives actors rights over payment and consent when digital replicas are used
Actors in the UK are to be given more rights over their “digital replicas” as part of a new agreement on AI protections with TV and film producers, secured after a growing on-set backlash.
Under a wide-ranging new deal secured by Equity, the actors’ union, performers will have the rights to be paid when their digital replicas are used and to consent to whether their digital replica is used or not.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Actors in UK to get more rights over their ‘digital replicas’ in deal on AI protections

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
About a third of cases involved chemicals banned for use on EU farms, according to investigation by Unearthed and Public Eye 
Pesticides sold by European chemical companies were named in more than 1,600 poisoning reports in Brazil last year, an investigation has found.
About a third of the cases involved chemicals banned from use on farms in the EU because of the risks they pose to people and the environment. But European companies are not banned from manufacturing these chemicals, as long as they export them overseas to countries where they are legally allowed to be used.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: European-made pesticides named in 1,605 poisoning reports in Brazil last year

articles.author: Emine Sinmaz
articles.description:
Comments come after Mia Latter, who alleged she was raped by Russell Brand, had said she wanted a change in law
A woman who has accused David Walliams of grooming her has said she supports a staggered age of consent.
Walliams, 55, has been accused of using his power and celebrity status to prey on young women and teenagers for sex, a joint investigation by the Guardian and ITV News has found.
Support for anyone affected by sexual abuse issues is available in the UK from Rape Crisis on 0808 500 2222 in England and Wales, 0808 801 0302 in Scotland, or 0800 0246 991 in Northern Ireland. The National Association for People Abused in Childhood (Napac) offers support for adult survivors on 0808 801 0331. Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. Other international helplines are available for people affected by sexual abuse, childhood abuse, and people in crisis.
The ITV News documentary David Walliams: Power and Silence is available to watch on YouTube and ITVX.
 Continue reading...
